explicit: persistent expanded state in virtual lists
symptoms: A long scrolling list feels stuck on mobile, with each row catching touch for 100-300 ms instead of scrolling smoothly. A long-press menu may trigger while the user is trying to scroll upward. Buttons appear unresponsive for a fraction of a second after tap, so the user taps again and the action happens twice. A drawer opens like a side panel, but the user still sees and interacts with the underlying screen. Returning to a collapsed list or drawer resets scroll position, selection, or virtualization cache. Jumping to a distant item in a long list animates painfully or janks for seconds, making the app feel frozen.

A mobile chat or history view takes too long to become interactive because the main thread is blocked by rendering too many entries at once. The user sees duplicate outgoing bubbles because the client optimistically inserts a message and then receives the same event from the server broadcast. A header becomes ambiguous because primary state is buried in the wrong area, so the user cannot tell what model, effort, or context is active. A read-only or special-mode banner steals too much vertical space on a small screen and should be replaced with subtler header-level signaling. A previewable file or attachment opens as a full route instead of a quick bottom sheet, breaking spatial context.
